effect_summary: A completeness-aware contiguous immutable-certificate chain rejects declared partial listing, unreadable newest evidence, and conflicting forks in the tested symbolic model, but cannot prove freshness when the entire certificate set is silently rolled back and presented as complete. Immutable certificates therefore remain integrity evidence rather than an absolute monotone freshness witness; this slice does not pass Phase-1 acceptance.
exact_tested_scope: One deterministic three-generation certificate chain with six cases: complete current listing, declared prefix truncation, identical duplicate same-generation certificate, conflicting fork, unreadable newest certificate, and whole-certificate-set rollback claimed complete.
conflict_check: Semantic inputs were limited to exact frozen sanitized controls, exact neuroscience role config, own neuroscience LATEST/preflight, and one deterministic local symbolic model. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, protected-primary, public-source, hosted-compute, paid, finite-credit, manual-user, or scheduler semantics were used.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: checkpoint first, then execute exactly one freshness-free state-reconstruction probe. Model a stale pointer replay over a content-addressed/idempotency-keyed durable effect interface and compare it with a non-idempotent irreversible effect. Test crash before commit, crash after effect before pointer update, stale-old-valid replay, duplicate retry, and destination record rollback. Accept only outcome classes where stale reconstruction cannot duplicate/corrupt the durable effect without any external monotone witness, richer-mode/protected/manual execution, finite monthly quota, same-run polling/backoff, or incremental cost; classify the rest as still requiring an external freshness witness.
